answer: Proof of useful computation acts as a gatekeeper, forcing nodes to solve resource-intensive tasks to gain network entry. An attacker must expend significant power to bypass this, much like a traveler seeking a hidden inlet through an ivory tower. By illuminating malicious activity with a cryptographic lantern, the network forces an economic cost on each identity, ensuring that flooding the system with fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive and computationally unsustainable for any bad actor.
